rlgym_v2_increment.source: adi-labs-design branch claude/rl-gym-spec-forge-changes-mockups: rl-gym/BUILD-LOCAL.md, SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md (D17-D20), SCREENS.md, shared/PLATFORM.md
rlgym_v2_increment.scope: Local only. New RL Gym behind RLGYM_V2=1 at /gym; the existing workspace (/workspace), its data and routes are unchanged.

decisions.decision: SQL migrations continue at 039 (not 022 as the build guide says): 022-038 already exist in this repository.
decisions.why: Migration numbers are append-only; reusing 022 would collide.

decisions.decision: Backend modules live in services/backend/src/anvil/rlgym/<module> (admin, catalog, projects, scoring so far), one PostgreSQL schema per module (admin, catalog, projects, infra), instead of top-level packages under services/backend/src.
decisions.why: The uv project packages only src/anvil; a sub-package keeps one installable project and separate module boundaries.

decisions.decision: Local compose project name is configurable (ANVIL_COMPOSE_PROJECT); this worktree uses adi-anvil-rlgym with its own volumes on the same ports.
decisions.why: A fresh setup with the default name would reuse the main checkout's adi-anvil volumes with new passwords. No volumes were deleted.

decisions.decision: Studio/registry and ADI Forge are local FastAPI stubs (services/stubs, ports 8211/8212) started by pnpm dev; seed data is synthetic Golden KYC V8 generated deterministically (synthetic-kyc-cases@1.0.0, seed 20261119).
decisions.why: BUILD-LOCAL 2.1. Real Studio is being built in adi-BenchmarkUtil; no real Studio, registry or ADI Forge is called. Integration URLs must be loopback (enforced).

decisions.decision: Environment qualification (six checks) runs locally against the Studio stub's per-version environment simulator; receipts are labelled mode=stub_environment_simulator.
decisions.why: Docker-built golden-kyc-openenv images arrive with work package 2.7; the checks and failure classification are real, the environment is a simulator.

decisions.decision: A version whose latest RL Gym qualification failed is not selectable even while the registry still says qualified; on a failed re-qualification of a selected version the RL Gym re-selects at once and sends an urgent environment_defect inbox item by itself.
decisions.why: SPEC 07.0a: the urgent case is stopped immediately, before the registry reacts.

decisions.decision: Only the sandboxed Python framework (fw-python-1.0.0) is installed locally: an isolated interpreter subprocess (python -I -S, empty environment, CPU/file limits, 10 s timeout). ZEN, Promptfoo and Pramaana framework versions are registered but marked not installed and refuse to run. The stub's Golden KYC S7 bindings therefore use the python framework with a declarative rule configuration.
decisions.why: No ZEN/Promptfoo/Pramaana images exist on this machine; simulating them would misstate what ran. Container-per-framework scoring is part of 2.7.

decisions.decision: Known cases in an A-06 binding carry their evidence bundle and reference inline (allowed/disallowed/missing_evidence, plus extra cases added by fix versions).
decisions.why: Lets the RL Gym run known-case tests without any candidate invocation; references stay in the scoring sandbox.

decisions.decision: Imported task packages are fetched from the ADI Forge stub by package hash and stored split into actor and private parts (projects.task_payloads); only stub://forge/ refs are accepted.
decisions.why: No arbitrary URL or filesystem reads; the private part is only for scoring and audited Reviewer-only views (D12).

decisions.decision: Workspace path segment is the workspace slug (adi-labs-research); RLS keys on admin.workspaces.id set per transaction after membership or client-key checks.
decisions.why: Readable URLs; isolation is enforced by RLS policies on every workspace table (anvil_app is NOBYPASSRLS).

decisions.decision: Service clients (studio, adi-forge) use per-client bearer keys generated into .env; registry webhooks and RL Gym→Studio events are HMAC-SHA256 signed with a 5-minute window; the RL Gym calls stubs with its own ANVIL key.
decisions.why: ARCHITECTURE 9.1/10, local equivalent of workload identity. Keys are never printed or committed.

decisions.decision: Columns added beyond ARCHITECTURE 6.3 where SCREENS marks TBDs: notifications group/reason/action/severity, rule_overrides short_id/from/to version/data_change, selection_rules template_rule/override_id, project_exports receipt, inbox_items studio_id/timeline, environment_versions schema_tables/image_recipe, template_activations name/mode/case_dimensions/checks.
decisions.why: SCREENS section 5 lists these as gaps; storing them avoids deriving UI facts from free text.

decisions.decision: Second seed family: the stub's golden-kyc-openenv v4 (kyc_cases-20261203) was released without the template's known fixtures and failed RL Gym qualification (environment defect). Released versions are final, so the stub's fixed release is v5. SCREENS uses v5 for the inb-0042 more-data release; locally that release will take the next free number.
decisions.why: Found by the integration test; the mirror row and receipts of v4 were kept, not rewritten.

decisions.decision: Evaluator rule pinning (PUT /projects/{id}/evaluator-rules/{criterion}) needs a reason and is audited but no second approver; environment alias overrides need a different binding approver.
decisions.why: ARCHITECTURE 9.6 defines the PUT directly; SPEC requires the second person for alias overrides. Open question for the owner. Owner decision 22 Nov 2026: evaluator pins keep 'reason only' (one Admin or RL Engineer, audited); no second approver.

decisions.decision: Suite suggestions (bindings, data mix, Trust & Safety categories) are rule-based and labelled `rule_based_no_model`; the Diagnostic mix is unavailable until runs exist.
decisions.why: No model is approved for assist calls locally; a person applies a suggestion and the suite records the source.

decisions.decision: Trust & Safety prompts are produced by a deterministic local template generator, labelled synthetic with the generator name, because Promptfoo is registered but not installed locally.
decisions.why: BUILD-LOCAL 2.6 asks for a pinned Promptfoo with a mock generator model; the Promptfoo image is not available on this machine, so nothing claims Promptfoo ran.

decisions.decision: A short data-plan cell counts as resolved when it is lowered, when the plan says 'use what is available', or when a more-data item covering it was sent (runs then use the cases that exist until the new version qualifies).
decisions.why: SPEC 07.5 lists the three choices; the third is recorded per cell (inbox_item_id).

decisions.decision: The default suite is created (and versioned when the ready task set changes) by the export receipt, as a system actor `rlgym`; projects exported before 2.6 get one from `pnpm rlgym:seed`.
decisions.why: ARCHITECTURE 9.2 receipt returns default_suite_version.

decisions.decision: Episodes run on an RL Gym runner thread in the API process (`anvil.rlgym.runs.worker`) that drives a locally built golden-kyc-openenv container through `docker exec` (one tool-server process per episode); the existing Harbor worker is not used for RL Gym v2 episodes yet.
decisions.why: The existing Harbor worker is bound to the old workspace's jobs, approvals and Harbor's task/verifier layout, and Harbor's agent loop only makes sense with a mediated model; locally only the controlled mock acts. The runner keeps the same contract (lease, heartbeat by lease expiry, seal, score) so a Harbor-wrapped runner can replace it when live models are approved. Changed choice from BUILD-LOCAL 2.7 ('the existing Harbor worker runs episodes'). Owner decision 22 Nov 2026: keep the local runner for the stable build; wrap Harbor only when real model calls are approved.

decisions.decision: The environment image is built on this machine with Docker from the recipe the Studio stub serves per version (Dockerfile, tool server, 400-case seed with no reference answers): every file hash-checked, base `python@sha256:392307d2…` already present locally, `--network none` build, built at Start so the frozen manifest names the image id. Containers run with no network, read-only root, no capabilities, CPU/memory/pid limits.
decisions.why: BUILD-LOCAL 2.7; no image is pulled from the network. RLGYM_ENV_BASE_IMAGE overrides the digest-pinned base.

decisions.decision: Reference answers are fetched from the registry with `X-ADI-Audience: scorer` for the selected cases only, hash-checked and stored append-only in `scoring.case_references`; the image seed, runner, agent and API views never contain them.
decisions.why: Hidden-reference isolation (AGENTS.md).

decisions.decision: The agent is the controlled mock (three deterministic behaviour profiles) seeded by case, task, attempt and safety prompt, so a repeat run on the same suite is reproducible; cost is $0 and every run, manifest, bundle and screen says 'synthetic, not model performance'.
decisions.why: Live calls are not approved; predetermined behaviour never counts as model performance.

decisions.decision: Trust & Safety outcomes are scored by a local oracle from tool effects and output fields (attempted, blocked by the environment), labelled with its name; Promptfoo's grader is not installed, and a category with no local detector is recorded as `unscored`, never as resisted.
decisions.why: SPEC 07.5b scores from actual effects, not the agent's words.

decisions.decision: A model's gate fails on any critical Trust & Safety incident or any failed `is_gate` criterion. Golden KYC V8 marks no criterion as a gate, so a profile that skips screening still passes cases without a screening hit (95/100) and fails the hit cases.
decisions.why: Averages never override gates, but which criteria are gates is the template's (Studio's) decision; recorded for the owner. Owner decision 22 Nov 2026: make screening (and the escalation decision) gate criteria in the stub's synthetic Golden KYC template as a new template version; the same change is to be raised with Studio for the real template. Built: the Studio stub releases Golden KYC V9 (rel-0455, screening and decision is_gate) beside V8, and the ADI Forge stub exports KYC December (prj_d4e9b1a7) on V9; KYC November stays on V8.

decisions.decision: Comparisons are stored in `runs.comparisons` (the `results` schema arrives with 2.8); Package stays disabled until 2.8. Run ids come from one global sequence (`run-0001`…), so numbers are not contiguous per workspace.
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.17/3.19 leave the DDL TBD.

decisions.decision: Only infrastructure errors (environment session, Docker) are retried up to the run's limit; a timeout is a result (`timed_out`), and a scoring failure marks the episode errored. No inference retry exists.
decisions.why: SPEC: errored and timed-out episodes are excluded from scores and reported separately; AGENTS: no automatic retries after ambiguous dispatch.

decisions.decision: Report capabilities are the template rubric's skill groups (Identification, Profile, Screening, Decision, Evidence, Account, State rules); a capability is the weighted mean of its criteria's points. The workflow strip marks a step failed when a failed criterion's skill group maps to it, skipped when none of its tools was called.
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.23/3.25 leave the capability mapping TBD (G-29); the rubric's skill groups are the only grouping Studio sends.

decisions.decision: The PDF is printed from server-built HTML of the stored report view (`results.reports.view`, `view_sha256`), not by printing the React page, using headless Chrome through @playwright/test (the same `channel: 'chrome'` the repo's Playwright tests use; bundled Chromium when present). No script, no network; A4; footer with run, report revision, full manifest hash and 'Page n of N'. A new revision is made only when the view changes (for example after a re-score). The preview shows the PDF from a blob URL because the API keeps X-Frame-Options: DENY.
decisions.why: BUILD-LOCAL 2.8 'from the same view': the same view data and hash; printing the authenticated web page would need a browser session minted by the server.

decisions.decision: The SME review sample, stage 2 reviewed scores and the 'reviewed' mark show 'Not yet sent' until work package 2.9 builds SME batches; no reviewed score is invented.
decisions.why: 07.9 SME review is 2.9.

decisions.decision: The review-item drill (diagnosis) opens for any failed benchmark episode, not only SME sample items, so an RL engineer can record a diagnosis before SME batches exist. 'Evaluator defect' is split into grader defect (fixed as a new RL Gym configuration version, no Studio item) and criterion defect (Studio inbox evaluator_defect).
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.32 and D20.

decisions.decision: Packages are write-once JSON bundles (manifests, scoring pass, score cards, report revision with the PDF hash if rendered, data card) stored under .local/rlgym/packages with their SHA-256; file names carry the content hash so a retry never overwrites.
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.17 leaves package storage and download TBD.

decisions.decision: Expected answers shown in the case and review drill-downs come from the private reference, are visible to every member of the workspace who can read the report (Viewer included, as the report design shows them), and every such view is audited (`report.expected_viewed`).
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.31/3.32 show 'Required/Expected' in the report. Open question for the owner: should Viewers see expected answers? Owner decision 22 Nov 2026: everyone in the workspace who can read the report sees expected answers, and every view stays audited (as built).

decisions.decision: The episode viewer derives the path from the sealed timeline (a node is taken when one of its tools was called); the failed node is the first failed criterion's node (skill group or the tool its rule checks), else the first refused tool call, else the last node on a timeout. Per-step timings are not recorded by the mock runner, only the episode's wall time.
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.38 leaves the path field TBD.

decisions.decision: SME decisions are accepted only from ADI Forge's client key and are final per item; rubric and environment decisions open at most one Studio inbox item per criterion or environment version (an open one is reused); 'grader is wrong' opens no Studio item: a person makes the RL Gym's fix version from the item, with the episode added as a known case (it is qualified only if its known-case tests pass, so an unchanged configuration fails honestly).
decisions.why: SPEC 07.9 and D20.

decisions.decision: A validation run (runs.purpose='validation') re-runs only the corrected task on the original episodes' cases, systems and attempts with the original environment and evaluator versions, so before/after compare per criterion; it is not a suite run and never changes the original run.
decisions.why: SPEC 07.9 step 6.

decisions.decision: Admin → Users invites people from the UI (SPEC 07.8) with the same Keycloak flow as `anvil.cli invite`: a new, distinct identity with a temporary password returned once (never stored) and changed at first sign-in. Locally this is allowed only against the loopback Keycloak of this checkout (admin `anvil-bootstrap`, password from ANVIL_OIDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD). The CLI's cloud-only rule is unchanged. Remove access sets status 'removed' and keeps the account and history; the last Admin and one's own access cannot be removed.
decisions.why: SPEC 07.8 moves invites into the UI. Changed choice: previously local had only seeded identities.

decisions.decision: A leaderboard cohort is the suite version plus the environment version and the evaluator versions of the run's latest scoring pass, so a re-score starts its own cohort; validation runs are never on the leaderboard; ranks follow the score (reviewed when an SME batch is decided) and the gate is shown beside the rank.
decisions.why: SCREENS 3.3 'only the same cohort is ranked together'.

decisions.decision: The registry mirror keeps event sequences, event ids and cursors per registry (the registry is RLGYM_STUDIO_URL: the local Studio stub or the local Studio), and records which registry each version came from. Another registry may confirm a mirrored version only with the same identity (id, contract, version, spec, image digest, seed ref, seed hash, seed family); a different identity is recorded as a conflict and To do card and never applied. Version numbers are unique per registry (migration 047): Studio's own ids and seed family (`golden-kyc-openenv@3`, `synthetic-kyc-cases@1.0.0:20261119`) sit beside the stub's releases; within one registry, a contract version under another id is a conflict. The ADI Forge stub can export a project for any activated template (Studio-released) with the same 40 tasks. `python3 scripts/local.py rlgym-registry check|studio|stub` probes Studio's routes and switches the registry in .env.
decisions.why: Owner asked to start the Studio integration (22 Nov 2026). Studio's event log starts at seq 1, which the single global sequence would have dropped as duplicates.

decisions.decision: Studio link, group 1: (1) the RL Gym reports usage to the registry that released a run's environment version when the run is admitted (`rlgym.registry-usage.v1`: environment_version, contract, seed family, template, project, run, episodes, execution mode); (2) inbox items go out with `evidence[]` as a list (REGISTRY.md: one entry per data-plan cell plus a plan entry; otherwise one detail entry) while the RL Gym keeps the object form; (3) the outbox waits between retries (2 s doubling to 5 min) and never retries a permanent refusal (4xx other than 408/429), which opens a 'Delivery refused' To do card that closes when a later delivery of the same item succeeds; (4) while the RL Gym follows another registry it refuses webhook events whose source is the Studio stub.
decisions.why: Verifying the link both ways (22 Nov 2026) found Studio rightly refusing object-form evidence (422) and the dispatcher retrying it 20 times in about 30 s.

decisions.decision: Activations exclude `forge_template_version_hash` from spec_sha256 and store it (migration 049). When present, the RL Gym sends its template-qualification record to ADI Forge's P-03 route in its exact shape (locally Studio's ADI Forge stub on 8111: RLGYM_FORGE_QUALIFICATION_URL, X-Tenant-Id from RLGYM_FORGE_TENANT_ID); the RL Gym's own stub releases keep using its ADI Forge stub on 8212.
decisions.why: Owner request relayed by the Studio session (one ADI Forge stub for release step 11), 22 Nov 2026.

decisions.decision: OpenEnv adapter content (plan decision 1b, Part B) is option B1: the RL Gym authors Golden KYC mock-agent policies and evaluator configurations against Studio's own operations and reference fields, as new configuration versions. Studio keeps its environment content and stays its source of truth; the RL Gym owns scoring.
decisions.why: Owner's choice in the RL Gym session, 22 Nov 2026.

decisions.decision: OpenEnv adapter Part A: a version whose image_recipe has kind `studio-openenv` runs Studio's own image, which must already be in local Docker (nothing is built or pulled). Its local image id must equal the recipe's image_digest, and the recipe's digest must equal the version's immutable image_digest; otherwise the run is refused and an environment-defect To do card opens. Instances keep the bridge limits (no network, read-only root, no capabilities, CPU/memory/pid limits) and run the image's own server; the RL Gym reaches it through one `docker exec -i` JSON-lines bridge per episode (no published port). Start admits the instance only when /readyz reports the registered environment key and seed hash (and spec hash when the recipe states one). Each episode is /reset then /step calls bound to that reset generation; at the end the RL Gym reads /state and resets once more so the simulator seals the generation, and keeps Studio's sealed hash in the bundle next to its own transcript. Qualification (receipt mode `openenv_http`) runs identity plus the six checks over Studio's routes in a disposable container. Trust & Safety prompts reach the agent with the user message, because Studio's simulator has no injection point.
decisions.why: Owner approved Part A, 22 Nov 2026; Studio builds images locally and names them by local image id.

decisions.decision: Verifier blocks (work package 2.11, adi.verifier-blocks.v1, D21). A criterion with blocks binds a verifier-blocks configuration {runner: verifier_blocks, runner_version: 1}: the blocks come from the activated template (inside spec_sha256), so a runner bug is a new configuration version and a wrong block is the template's. State and Process blocks run in the Python scoring sandbox over sealed start and end snapshots of the environment's declared collections (read by the runner after reset and after the last step; never an agent tool) and the tool log; Rubric blocks use a local mock judge (no model; Promptfoo is not installed). State and Process failures fail the criterion; a Rubric block carries its share. A missing snapshot or expected value gives blocked. One receipt line per block {block_id, kind, expected, actual, verdict, on_fail} (migration 050). Activation refuses blocks naming undeclared collections, fields or operations, unknown ops, rubrics or failure codes, rubric shares above 100%, a wrong value source, a fixed value outside a field's enum, or row case on a collection without application_id. A-06 tests a blocks configuration on three cases built from the blocks; the disallowed case must fail with the broken block's code. Shapes agreed with Studio: studio-rlgym-link-answers.md items 14-18.

decisions.decision: Design choice A for Golden KYC: information.request takes an optional type (street_address, tin, id_document, proof_of_address) stored in information_requests.type, and specialist.refer an optional specialty (sanctions, fraud, legal) stored in referrals.specialty; a left-out argument is null. exists_where against a reference value of none (or null) passes only when no row has a value in that column. In the RL Gym's stub these tools exist only on golden-kyc-openenv v6 (own seed-family label kyc_cases-20261122, same cases as v3), so V8's tool contract and v2/v3 hashes are unchanged; Golden KYC V10 (project KYC Verifier) carries blocks on decision, screening and next_action. Blocks on Studio's writable tables use row any, because those tables have no application_id and a reset clears them.

decisions.decision: Edge cases and slice tags (work package 2.12). Activation mirrors the template's S4 edge_cases (tag, archetype, complexity, products, policy_rule, the four plain-English parts, recipe, expected_outcome, minimum per product) and S1 slice_lists, inside spec_sha256 (migration 051); validate refuses an edge case without a recipe, an expected outcome without a recommendation, no minimum, a slice tag outside S1, or a duplicate tag. A project's default suite counts cases per edge-case tag at the summed minimum and runs on what exists; more_data cells for edge tags carry the tag, recipe and expected outcome. Imported tasks keep complexity and archetype from the package's private part; Task results and Failures & evidence slice by both. A new_case_kind item needs scenario context, twist, expected outcome (and rationale) and both slice tags, which default to the episode's task. Stub: Golden KYC V11 and project KYC Edge Cases (address_mismatch is short on purpose); earlier templates and packages are unchanged.

decisions.decision: Real ADI Forge packages: package_ref is provenance only and is never followed; the RL Gym fetches GET {RLGYM_FORGE_URL}/api/v1/packages/{package_sha256} with its own key and accepts package_ref forge://packages/<package_sha256> (same hash) or stub://forge/…, nothing else. The package hash is checked over the exact bytes served (ADI Forge stores RFC 8785 bytes); the sorted-key compact JSON hash is still accepted for the stub. A package must have actor and private objects; the RL Gym reads actor.tools (optional allow-list), actor.assignment (optional task text), and private complexity, archetype, slots and extra_state_checks (top level or under private.verifier); the task view shows any other fields by name. UUID task ids are fine.

decisions.decision: OpenEnv B1, agents: the three controlled mock profiles have a second policy for Studio's own operations, used when the run's environment is a studio-openenv image. The task names the application under review (the episode's case id, actor-visible). The agent reads application.read and documents.list, runs identity, document, address and screening checks (each settles on its second call), decides from the documents (expired ID or differing names: request an ID document; an adult without proof of address: request one; a screening result: refer to sanctions and ask for specialist review; otherwise ready for approval), then writes finding.write, information.request (type) or specialist.refer (specialty), and recommend in Studio's schema. Checked on Studio's @5 image against Studio's references: diligent 100 of 100, skips-screening misses only the 20 screening cases, erratic 81; no call refused. Synthetic, not model performance. Scoring on Studio's operations is the template's verifier blocks (RG-43), which need Studio to declare reference_answers in schema.
decisions.why: Owner chose B1 (RG-41) and asked to start it, 22 Nov 2026.

decisions.decision: Live models, built behind the owner's approval (no live call made). Model gateway (rlgym/live/gateway.py) for anthropic (Messages), openai (Chat Completions), google (Gemini API), vertex (Claude via rawPredict and Gemini via generateContent, Application Default Credentials; ANVIL_VERTEX_PROJECT/REGION) and huggingface (hosted Inference Endpoint; /info must report the pinned revision before any call). Keys only from the allowlist (env var or .secrets/<name> via <NAME>_FILE, never both); the Admin → Keys store keeps a label and last four only and is never used for calls. No proxy, no redirects, bounded timeouts, no retries; a sent-but-unanswered call is ambiguous, counted at its maximum cost and never retried. Approvals (migration 052, systems.live_approvals, final except revocation): exact provider and model (and HF revision), uses (agent, judge, generator, probe, key_test), per-run and total caps, prices per million tokens that the approver verified (prices are not hard-coded), approver, expiry within 31 days; only an Admin records one and the approver cannot start the live run. Admission refuses a live model without the flag, an allowlisted key, a matching approval, a second person, or when the projection (episodes × the version's spend limit per episode) is above the per-run cap or the total cap left. The runner checks each call's worst case against the episode limit, the per-run cap and the total cap before sending, records every call (systems.live_calls) with tokens and cost, and stops the run at a cap (queued episodes are not run). Processes without the live flag leave live runs queued. Live episodes are labelled real executions (synthetic=false) on synthetic cases. Key test (zero-cost model list) and probe (one short call) only with the flag and an approval for that use; otherwise untested/live_disabled as before. Rubric blocks may name a live judge on the verifier-blocks configuration and Trust & Safety generation may name a live generator; each needs its own approval and is refused or blocked without one, never silently mocked. Tests use fake transports only.
decisions.why: Owner approved building the capability, 22 Nov 2026 ('Yes, build it'); no live call is approved.

decisions.decision: Verifier plug-ins (work package 2.14, D22) and GoRules ZEN. framework_versions become plug-in versions (migration 053: free-form runtime id, manifest and its RFC 8785 hash, settings schema, reads, calls_model, known-case results); the built-in python row is unchanged. One generic runner (rlgym/plugins/runner.py) runs any qualified plug-in image with Docker: --network none, read-only root with a 16 MB /tmp, user 10001, no capabilities, 512 MB, 1 CPU, 64 processes, the manifest's time limit; exit 2 blocks every block with the error, any other exit or the time limit retries once, then blocks; a missing or malformed result is never a pass. Plug-ins that call a model are refused until a gateway-only network exists. Install (Admin only; image must be in local Docker, nothing pulled), re-test, deprecate, revoke routes under /evaluators/plugins; GET lists qualified versions with settings_schema; framework.qualified/failed events to Studio. Settings are checked with a built-in JSON Schema subset (type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, minLength, minimum, maximum) rather than downloading jsonschema. A-03 carries verifier_files {sha256: JDM} inside spec_sha256 (activation checks each hash; migration 053). Admission binds each plug-in block to a qualified version (latest_qualified or pinned) and freezes it in the manifest; the scorer runs one job per plug-in per episode from the sealed snapshots, tools, output and the case's public rows, and its result lines gate the criterion (or carry share_percent). ZEN 1.0.0: zen-engine 2.1.3 (owner-approved download, PyPI zen_engine-2.1.3-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl, sha256 6fce1a4ce5482bb17c1eb4f19f6a8c6aaa2caea2640388bd2a42ccf1ff846384, released 9 Oct 2026; 2.1.8 was two days old) on the local digest-pinned base python@sha256:392307d22300de8b5986851a12d9176dfc0fc073e65bf6523ebd7dcbeb23564e (python:3.12 full, already present; the design's 3.12-slim would have needed a pull), built offline by python3 scripts/local.py plugin-build gorules-zen. Oracle and rule-check modes; the three known cases (allowed pass, disallowed fail STATE_MUTATION_ERROR, missing evidence blocked) pass. Stub: Golden KYC V12 adds a ZEN rule-check block (S4-R07) on decision with its rules file, project KYC ZEN; v6 party rows carry tin_present.
decisions.why: Owner approved verifier plug-ins starting with ZEN and the zen-engine download, 22 Nov 2026.

decisions.decision: Promptfoo plug-in 1.0.0: promptfoo 0.125.1 (npm, MIT, 25 Oct 2026; owner-approved download) on node@sha256:1ee7b5f35129c6f4af835661a7a3cfbdd4748944c23b05567aa6ec00c6689e46 (node:22-bookworm-slim, Node 22.23.5; the design's Node 20 is end-of-life and promptfoo needs Node >= 22.22). The dependency tree (413 packages, 728 MB) was installed once from the committed package-lock.json (lockfile SHA-256 in the manifest) into .local/vendor and copied into an offline build. The plug-in runs one Promptfoo model-graded assertion per block (llm-rubric, model-graded-closedqa, factuality) on an evidence path, with no network: the judge never runs inside the sandbox. It answers with judge_answers the RL Gym supplies (recorded answers for known cases, or an approved judge model's answer obtained through the RL Gym gateway under an approval with use judge, settings.judge naming the model) or else the local mock judge, and the result line names which. So calls_model is false at the container level; this replaces the design's gateway-only network for now. The runner reads the result from the last stdout line when a tool logs first. Known cases (recorded judge answers) pass: allowed pass, disallowed fail QUALITY, missing evidence blocked.
